pins.title: Cold Plunge vs Red Light Therapy for Sleep: Which Suits an Evening Routine?
pins.subtitle: Winding down vs an alertness spike
pins.description: Recovering at night? Some people report red light in the evening feels more compatible with winding down, since it skips the alertness spike linked to cold exposure. Responses vary, and neither tool replaces good sleep habits. Our guide matches each tool to your main recovery goal, with safety notes on heart conditions and pregnancy. Not medical advice. #coldplunge #redlighttherapy #sleeproutine #eveningroutine #homerecovery

pins.title: Inflatable Cold Plunge Upkeep: Plan for Ice, Draining, and Water Care
pins.subtitle: What a no-plumbing tub asks of you
pins.description: An inflatable cold plunge needs no plumbing, but most budget models rely on ice rather than a built-in chiller, so you're buying ice or freezing water ahead. Add draining, cleaning, and water treatment. A red light panel mainly needs an occasional wipe-down. Talk to a doctor first if you have a heart condition or circulation issues, or are pregnant. Not medical advice. #coldplunge #icebath #apartmentliving #redlighttherapy #homerecovery
